Use markdown syntax for formatting instead of html. Html is not allowed/supported. For more tips and help, check out /v/css.

As Atko stated, you'll want to familiarize yourself with markdown syntax. That will allow you to give your sidebar basic formatting. Here's a link:

http://daringfireball.net/projects/markdown/syntax

It's the same syntax that is used in comments. One offhand tip about markdown I'd like to mention, is that if you want a proper hard line break, you need to add two spaces at the end of a line before pressing enter.

To get fancier than what markdown can provide, you'll need to add some CSS.

CSS is not really a programming language. It's more like a list of override switches. Every element of your sub (areas, banners, links, etc.) has default properties. With CSS those properties can be modified.

Legal Legacy Laws

This was part of a distribution system, that manufactures can not directly sell to the customers, and use dealerships as a buffer to both shape what a customer can buy, and to track statistics on how fast which specific cars are being traded in and if anything was broken on them.

Tesla could not get dealerships to stock their cars, due to various contracts and Legacy pressure (25% markup would price them right out of the market). so they sold directly to the consumers.
